passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related financial statement notes included in Part II of this report under the caption “Item 8 - Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.” We operate on a 52/53-week fiscal year, which ends on the last Sunday in May. Fiscal 2026, which ended May 31, 2026, consisted of 53 weeks; fiscal 2025, which ended May 25, 2025, consisted of 52 weeks; and fiscal 2027, which ends on May 30, 2027, will consist of 52 weeks. OVERVIEW OF OPERATIONS Our business operates in the full-service dining segment of the restaurant industry. At May 31, 2026, we owned and operated 2,202 restaurants through subsidiaries in the United States under the Olive Garden®, LongHorn Steakhouse®, Yard House®, Ruth’s Chris Steak House®, Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen®, The Capital Grille®, Chuy’s®, Seasons 52®, Eddie V’s Prime Seafood®, Bahama Breeze®, and The Capital Burger® trademarks. We own and operate all of our restaurants in the United States, except for four restaurants operating under contractual agreements, one restaurant that we jointly own with a third party and operate independently, and 87 franchised restaurants. We also have 80 franchised restaurants in operation located in Canada, Latin America, the Caribbean, Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. All intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. On July 14, 2025, we closed on the sale of the Olive Garden Canada Restaurants to Recipe. All gains and losses on disposition have been aggregated in impairments and disposal of assets, net on our consolidated statement of earnings. See Note 4 for additional information. At the closing, Darden and Recipe entered into an area development agreement and franchise agreements, pursuant to which Recipe will operate current and any new restaurants contemplated thereunder under the Olive Garden trade name and will pay royalties for use of the trade name. On our June 2025 earnings call, we announced the decision to explore strategic alternatives for the Bahama Breeze brand, which, at that time, included 28 company-owned restaurants and one franchised restaurant. As part of this review, we evaluated a potential sale of the brand as well as the conversion of certain restaurants to other Darden brands. On February 3, 2026, we announced the completion of this process and our decision to permanently close approximately half of the remaining Bahama Breeze restaurants, which we completed on or about April 5, 2026, and our expectation to convert the remaining restaurants to other Darden brands over the next 12–18 months. As of the end of fiscal 2026, we have completed one conversion. See Note 4 for additional information. On October 11, 2024, we acquired 100 percent of the equity interest of Chuy’s Holdings Inc. (“Chuy’s”) in an all-cash transaction of $649.1 million in total consideration, $613.7 million in net cash consideration, inclusive of $35.4 million of cash on Chuy’s balance sheet at closing. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Various risks and uncertainties could affect our business. Any of the risks described below or elsewhere in this report or our other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission could have a material impact on our business, financial condition or results of operations. It is not possible to predict or identify all risk factors. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also impair our business operations. Risks Relating to Inflation and Macroeconomic Disruption A failure to address cost pressures, including rising costs for commodities, labor, health care, and utilities used by our restaurants, and a failure to effectively deliver cost management activities and achieve economies of scale in purchasing could compress our margins and adversely affect our sales and results of operations. Our results of operations depend, in part, on our ability to anticipate and react to changes in the price and availability of food, ingredients, labor, health care, utilities, fuel, and other related costs over which we may have little control. We have experienced and may continue to experience higher than normal inflationary conditions with respect to most or all of these costs during fiscal 2026. Operating margins for our restaurants are subject to changes in the price and availability of food commodities, including beef, pork, chicken, seafood, cheese, butter, and produce. The introduction of, or changes to, tariffs or adverse impacts resulting from restrictive trade policies or trade disputes on imported food products, such as produce and seafood, could increase our costs and possibly impact the supply of those products. We cannot predict whether we will continue to be able to anticipate and react to changing food costs by adjusting our purchasing practices, menu offerings, and menu prices, and a failure to do so could adversely affect our operating results. We seek to leverage our size to achieve economies of scale in purchasing, but there can be no assurances that we can always do so effectively. We are also subject to the general risks of inflation and its impact on the macroeconomic environment. Increases in minimum wage, health care, and other benefit costs may have a material adverse effect on our labor costs. We operate in many states and localities where the minimum wage is significantly higher than the federal minimum wage. The market for labor in the United States is competitive and has resulted in pressure on wages and may continue to do so in the future. Increases in minimum wage and market pressure may also result in increases in the wage rates paid for non-minimum wage positions. Many states and localities are also passing laws regulating employment practices and working conditions, which could have a material adverse effect on our labor costs in those areas. credit_strengths.text: Darden's full-service dining portfolio spans Olive Garden, LongHorn and specialty brands, generating revenue growth across the last three fiscal years. Operating margin sits modestly below the sector median, yet absolute operating income expanded, reflecting scale purchasing and menu pricing that partially offset commodity and labor inflation disclosed in the risk factors.

Gross and net leverage remain comfortably below the sector median, with net leverage near the lower quartile. Interest coverage exceeds the sector median by a wide margin, and the debt stack is entirely fixed-rate senior unsecured notes with no near-term bank maturities, supporting a minimal indicative financial risk profile.

key_risks.text: The risk factors flag sustained inflationary pressure on beef, produce, seafood, labor and health care, with limited ability to pass through menu pricing without harming guest traffic. Because restaurants are company-owned, cost inflation flows directly to margins, and any failure to achieve purchasing economies of scale could compress operating income and weaken coverage.

The debt note shows a large senior note maturing within the next fiscal year, plus another maturity the following year, while commercial paper is outstanding and supported by the revolver. Refinancing these maturities at higher rates would lift interest expense, and the leverage covenant limits incremental debt capacity if EBITDA declines.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating income covers gross interest expense many times over, and EBITDA comfortably exceeds total debt. With cash on hand and substantial revolver availability after commercial paper, liquidity supports scheduled maturities. However, operating cash flow is not available in the bundle, so free cash flow and its coverage of debt cannot be independently verified.

Capital expenditure is significant and, alongside dividends and buybacks, likely absorbs most internally generated cash. The current ratio is far below the sector median because current liabilities include the maturing senior note, a timing effect rather than a liquidity shortfall. Refinancing that maturity should restore a more normal working capital profile.

overall_credit_view.text: Darden presents a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with leverage below the sector median and coverage well above it. The business is cash-generative and the debt structure is unsecured fixed-rate notes. Our forward view is that leverage stays modest absent a large debt-funded acquisition or a material margin shock from cost inflation.

The principal credit considerations are refinancing the near-term note maturities, managing inflation-driven margin pressure, and funding shareholder returns without eroding liquidity. Because operating cash flow is missing, we cannot fully assess free cash flow coverage; obtaining that disclosure is material to confirming the current credit view.

credit_strengths.text: Darden 的全方位服務餐飲組合涵蓋 Olive Garden、LongHorn 及特色品牌，於過去三個財政年度均帶來收入增長。營業利潤率略低於行業中位數，但絕對營業利潤有所擴大，反映規模採購及菜單定價部分抵銷了風險因素中披露的商品及勞動力通脹。
總槓桿及淨槓桿均舒適地低於行業中位數，淨槓桿接近下四分位數。利息覆蓋率大幅高於行業中位數，且債務結構全為固定利率優先無抵押票據，並無近期銀行到期債務，支持極低的指示性財務風險狀況。

key_risks.text: 風險因素指出牛肉、農產品、海鮮、勞動力及醫療保健持續面臨通脹壓力，而透過菜單定價轉嫁成本的能力有限，否則會損害客流量。由於餐廳為公司自有，成本通脹直接影響利潤率，若未能實現採購規模經濟，可能壓縮營業利潤並削弱覆蓋率。
債務附註顯示一筆大額優先票據將於下一個財政年度內到期，另有一筆於其後一年到期，同時有商業票據在外流通並由循環信貸支持。以更高利率為該等到期債務再融資將增加利息支出，而槓桿契約限制倘 EBITDA 下降時的增量債務能力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營業利潤對總利息支出的覆蓋倍數甚高，且 EBITDA 舒適地超過總債務。憑藉手頭現金及商業票據後的大量循環信貸可用額度，流動性可支持預定到期債務。然而，營運現金流並未載於資料匯編中，故無法獨立核實自由現金流及其對債務的覆蓋。
資本開支龐大，連同股息及回購，可能吸收大部分內部產生現金。流動比率遠低於行業中位數，因流動負債包括即將到期的優先票據，此乃時間性影響而非流動性短缺。為該到期債務再融資應可恢復更正常的營運資金狀況。

overall_credit_view.text: Darden 呈現極低的指示性財務風險狀況，槓桿低於行業中位數，而覆蓋率則遠高於該水平。業務具現金生成能力，債務結構為無抵押固定利率票據。我們的前瞻觀點是，在沒有大規模債務融資收購或成本通脹導致重大利潤率衝擊的情況下，槓桿將維持溫和。
主要信用考量為為近期到期票據再融資、管理通脹驅動的利潤率壓力，以及在不會侵蝕流動性的情況下為股東回報提供資金。由於營運現金流缺失，我們無法全面評估自由現金流覆蓋；獲取該披露對確認當前信用觀點至關重要。
